title: Correlative Microscopy for 3D Structural Analysis of Dynamic Interactions
protocol: Glow discharge the carbon-side of a 200-mesh R2/2 Quantifoil gold EM finder grid under 25 mA for 25 seconds.
Float the EM grid, carbon-side down, onto a 40 μl droplet of 50 μg/ml fibronectin solution to coat it with fibronectin.
Disinfect the coated EM grid under UV light for 2 hours in a tissue culture hood.
Plate HeLa cells onto the grid at a density of 2 x 10^4 cells/ml, using a total volume of 2 ml culture.
Grow the plated cells at 37 °C with 5% CO2 in DMEM supplemented with L-glutamine and glucose, fetal calf serum, penicillin, and streptomycin for approximately 18 hours.
Add a fluorescent cell tracker (Red CMTPX) at a ratio of 1 μl per 2 ml into the glass-bottom culture dish.
Incubate the dish at 37 °C for 10 minutes to allow uptake of the fluorescent dye by the cells.
Wash the cells with PBS.
Add 50 μl pre-warmed fresh medium to the washed cells.
Place the dish onto the live-cell chamber, maintained at 37 °C, of a Swept Field Confocal scanner microscope.
Select multiple fields (10-15 positions) that contain 1-3 cells per square and are in phases between mitosis for optimal imaging.
Infect cells with VSV-G pseudo-typed HIV-1 particles containing GFP-Vpr.
Add 40 μl of a sample containing 40 ng/ml of p24 into the bottom of the dish without disturbing the EM grid.
Collect time-lapse high-speed 3D confocal images at previously selected positions for 20-40 min immediately after adding the virus particles.
Initiate and prepare the FEI Vitrobot (or other vitrification device) for plunge-freezing during collection of fluorescence confocal live-cell images.
Set the climate temperature of the vitrification device to 22 °C, target humidity to 100%, blotting time to 7 sec, and wait and drain time to 1 sec.
Place the grid storage box in the plunger dewar.
Prepare cold liquid ethane.
Mount the dewar onto the vitrification device.
Immediately after confocal live-cell imaging, place the culture dish onto an ice-cooled copper block.
Transfer the culture dish to the cryoEM sample preparation room.
Load the EM grid onto specialized tweezers.
Quickly blot away any media on the grid manually using filter paper.
Place 4 μl of 15 nm gold bead solution mixed with 0.2 μm fluorescent microspheres on the grid.
Instruct the device to blot and plunge freeze in liquid ethane.
Load the tweezers onto the vitrification device.
Set the blotting parameters: blot time, 7 sec; blot offset, 0; drain time, 1 sec; temperature, 22 °C; humidity, 100%.
Transfer the frozen-hydrated grid to a cryoEM holder for immediate imaging or storage in a liquid nitrogen dewar.
Fill a self-pressurized liquid nitrogen dewar with liquid nitrogen at least 2 hours before starting.
Mount a homebuilt cryo-fluorescence sample stage onto an inverted fluorescence light microscope.
Connect the liquid nitrogen inlet of the cryo-sample stage to the dewar.
Place the liquid nitrogen overflow protection outlet into an appropriate container.
Connect a dry nitrogen gas line to a sleeve over the objective lens.
Cool down and fill the copper chamber of the cryo-stage with liquid nitrogen through the inlet line from the dewar.
Transfer the grid storage box to the cooled-down cryo-stage when it reaches liquid nitrogen temperature.
Place the frozen-hydrated sample grid into the EM specimen cartridge on the copper block.
Clip the grid in place using a C-ring if using a Polara microscope cartridge.
Place a pre-cooled copper ring on top of the grid for easy retrieval after imaging if using a non-Polara cryo-electron microscope.
Place the cartridge with the grid into the inner chamber of the cryo-stage.
Search for the same virus particles from the live-cell imaging data.
Localize the identified particle on the EM grid using the index provided.
Acquire cryo-DIC and GFP images at the specified positions under cryo-conditions with a long working objective lens (2.7-4 mm).
Periodically check the liquid nitrogen level in the cryo-stage during fluorescence imaging and refill as needed to maintain the sample stage below -170 °C.
Upon completion of cryo-fluorescence imaging, return the specimen cartridge to the copper block platform and store it in a liquid nitrogen dewar for future cryoET analysis with a Polara system.
If using a non-Polara cryo-electron microscope, remove the copper ring after imaging and retrieve the sample grid.
Place the retrieved sample grid into a grid storage box.
Store the specimen in a liquid nitrogen dewar until it is examined by cryoET.
Overlap the acquired cryo-DIC and GFP images for data analysis.
Correlate the positions of the GFP signals in the cryo-fluorescence image with those obtained during live-cell imaging.
Load the sample cartridge into the cryo-transfer station of an electron microscope equipped with a field emission gun.
Operate under low-dose-search mode at 140X magnification to identify and save grid squares into a stage file.
Switch to low-dose-search mode at 3,500X magnification to insert a 100 μm objective aperture.
Search for and save positions correlated with GFP signals into a second stage file.
Under low-dose-exposure mode, find a blank area to adjust beam intensity to a dose of 1 or 2 e-/Å².
Refine the tilt axis by burning away ice in an unimportant carbon region using the stage y function.
Adjust the focus distance to ~3 μm under low-dose-focus mode.
Align the direction of focus parallel to the tilt axis under low-dose-focus mode.
Recall saved positions under low-dose-search mode and adjust the specimen eucentric height.
Check the tilt range for the area of interest under low-dose-search mode.
Acquire a projection image with very low electron dose (~1 e-/Å²) at 8 to 10 μm defocus in exposure mode.
Confirm correlated virus particles for cryo-electron tomography.
Switch to the low-dose-focus mode and proceed with automated eucentric height and focus functions on the focus area.
Set up parameters for acquiring a tilt-series.
Use tilt angles ranging ±70°, below and above 45°, at 3° increments below and 2° increments above.
Apply a defocus of 6 μm and a total dose of approximately 70 e-/Å².
Inspect the raw tilt series to adjust minimum and maximum density values.
Determine if any views need exclusion due to large image shifts.
Start eTomo and set up tomogram panel using axis type, pixel size, fiducial diameter, etc.
Create com scripts in eTomo.
Configure main window for simultaneous adjustment of stages of tomogram computation.
Modify necessary parameters and execute specific programs required by each processing step.
At the final stage, create a full aligned stack with a mean residual error less than 0.6.
Reconstruct tomograms using a weighted back-projection algorithm in IMOD.
Denoise potential areas of interest using a 3D nonlinear anisotropic diffusion edge enhancing program implemented in IMOD.
